document.abstract: The advantages of a streak camera having continuous receptivity and employing only one rotating element are discussed. The essential element of such a camera is a prism-mirror combination which is rotated at high speed. Various arrangements of this combination are possible, and have been investigated with a view to compensating for the aber-rational and “splitting” effects. The theory of image formation through the combination is reviewed and alternative schemes are discussed.
